query: For single-phase ZrB2 ceramic, which requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C and may lack the strength and structural integrity needed for service, what single intervention could lower the required preparation temperature and reduce the holes and eventual component failure caused by prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath? State one hypothesis identifying the intervention and its mechanism, predict its performance compared with conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2, define the relevant preparation and service boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and describe a controlled preparation, integrity, and long-duration exposure experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 5 wt % amorphous carbon to ZrB₂ powder will enable densification at ~2000 °C by carbothermal reduction of surface oxides, lowering the sintering temperature by ~300 °C and reducing residual porosity, thus improving structural integrity under prolonged liquid plating exposure.
generation.material_initial_state: Commercial ZrB₂ powder (1–10 µm, 1–2 wt % O₂, no sintering aid).
generation.intervention: Incorporate 5 wt % nano-amorphous carbon into the ZrB₂ powder prior to sintering.
generation.conditions: Spark plasma sintering under Ar, heating rate 100 °C/min, dwell 30 min at 2000 °C under 50 MPa (doped) vs 2300 °C for undoped control; plating bath exposure at 900 °C for 500 h in molten salt.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced ZrO₂ films at particle surfaces and grain boundaries enabling enhanced mass transport.
generation.mechanism: Amorphous carbon reacts with surface oxides (ZrO₂) to form CO/CO₂, cleaning grain boundaries and promoting diffusion, thus enabling full densification at lower temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: Doped ZrB₂ achieves ≥98 % theoretical density at 2000 °C with ≥50 % reduction in residual porosity vs control; after 500 h plating bath, doped specimens exhibit <1 % pore area fraction vs >5 % in control.
generation.baseline: Undoped ZrB₂ sintered at 2300 °C reaches ~95 % density and ~5 % residual pore volume; shows >5 % pore area fraction after 500 h plating bath.
generation.boundary: Sintering temperature 1800–2300 °C; carbon content 0–10 wt %; plating bath 800–1000 °C, exposure up to 1000 h.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty in optimal carbon fraction and exact densification kinetics under the chosen SPS conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of ZrB₂ specimens (pure and +5 wt % amorphous carbon). Sinter both via SPS under Ar at 2000 °C/30 min/50 MPa (doped) and 2300 °C/30 min/50 MPa (control). Measure density and porosity; then expose both to a 900 °C molten salt plating bath for 500 h. Characterize pore area fraction by SEM and micro-CT.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if carbon-doped ZrB₂ fails to reach ≥98 % theoretical density at 2000 °C or shows <30 % reduction in residual porosity vs control, or if post-bath pore area fraction in doped specimens is ≥ that of the control.
